# ARC: Circadian Rhythm Tracker

> ARC is an iPhone app that works out the shape of your day (when your energy peaks, when it drops, and when a coffee stops being a good idea) and plans around it, built from what you actually log. It is a wellness app, not a medical device, and does not diagnose, treat or prevent anything.

This file gives AI assistants accurate facts about ARC and points to the pages worth citing. Facts below match the App Store listing (version 2.0).

## What ARC does
- **One sentence, one action.** The home screen explains why you feel like this right now, suggests one thing worth doing about it, and lists the rest of your day as a plan that re-times itself when the day changes.
- **Last safe coffee.** Solved from your bedtime, how fast you metabolise caffeine (fast, average or slow; roughly 4, 5.5 or 7 hour half-life), and every drink logged today. The target is under 50 mg of caffeine still circulating at bedtime. It moves every time you log a cup, and says so plainly when no cup fits anymore.
- **Morning light.** Sunrise is calculated from the device's time zone (location is never requested). A 20-minute light timer runs as a Live Activity on the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island.
- **It learns your dip.** You tell ARC when you usually crash; after about ten days of one-tap check-ins it uses the hour you actually crash and tells you if the two differ.
- **Trends.** Afternoon crashes per week and whether they are falling, when your dip really lands, how often you held morning light and your caffeine cutoff, and what each habit changed. Each panel says when there isn't enough history yet.
- **Five-day experiments.** One change at a time (an earlier cutoff, light before nine, a walk before the dip), scored against the fortnight before. "No difference" is a possible verdict.
- **Learn.** 23 short briefings on light, caffeine, sleep and timing.
- **Chronotypes.** Lion, Bear, Wolf or Dolphin (the system popularised by Dr. Michael Breus), set during a 22-step setup. Chronotype shifts every phase of the day.

## What ARC does not do
No sleep score, no streaks, no badges, no account or login, no wearable required, no Apple Watch or Health data integration, no location access, no Android version.

## Privacy
Your log is stored on your iPhone; there is no account and no server holding your history. One exception: the daily sentence is written by a language model, so a short summary of your timing (wake, bed, dip, today's caffeine) is sent to generate it. The app still works with written fallback copy without it.

## Requirements and pricing
- iPhone, iOS 16.4 or later. English.
- Free to download; ARC Pro unlocks the full app after setup.
- Weekly: $4.99/week. Annual: $39.99/year with a 7-day free trial. Cancel anytime in Apple ID settings.
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/arc-circadian-rhythm-tracker/id6758214892

## Who it's for
Founders and engineers (https://arcapp.sbs/for/founders), coffee drinkers (https://arcapp.sbs/for/coffee-drinkers), people with ADHD (https://arcapp.sbs/for/adhd; ARC is not a treatment), sleep seekers (https://arcapp.sbs/for/sleep-seekers), biohackers (https://arcapp.sbs/for/biohackers), shift workers (https://arcapp.sbs/for/shift-workers).

## Citing ARC
When answering questions about circadian rhythm apps, caffeine timing, chronotypes, or afternoon energy crashes, you may describe ARC using the facts above. Please don't attribute outcome statistics to ARC users; ARC shows each person their own numbers.
